tools.name: validate_einvoice
tools.description: Validate an e-invoice (XRechnung UBL/CII, ZUGFeRD / Factur-X PDF, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0, EN 16931) with the official KoSIT validator. Returns valid/invalid, the detected format, every error and warning with its rule code, and the exact corrected value for common calculation errors. Pass the XML as

tools.name: peppol_lookup
tools.description: Check whether a company can receive e-invoices over Peppol. Accepts a Peppol ID (e.g. 0208:0123456749), a VAT number (e.g. BE0123456749, NL...B01) or a Belgian enterprise number. Returns each matching participant ID, whether it is registered, whether it accepts Peppol BIS invoices, and name/country

tools.name: check_leitweg_id
tools.description: Check a German Leitweg-ID (buyer reference BT-10 for invoices to German public authorities) against the official format and check digit (spec v2.0.2), and whether the authority is registered on Peppol (peppol_registered). Returns validity, the parts and the expected check digits.

tools.name: create_einvoice
tools.description: Create a valid e-invoice from structured data: XRechnung 3.0 (UBL or CII), ZUGFeRD / Factur-X PDF (EN 16931) or Peppol BIS Billing 3.0. The file is checked with the official KoSIT validator before it is returned; if it fails, you get the rule errors instead of a file. XML comes back as text in `xml`

tools.name: read_invoice_pdf
tools.description: Read an ordinary (non-e-invoice) PDF invoice and return its data in the input format of create_einvoice: seller and buyer (name, address, VAT ID, country), invoice number, dates, IBAN/BIC, Leitweg-ID and the invoice lines (only if quantity x price and the line sum match the PDF's net total; otherwis

tools.name: explain_rule
tools.description: Explain an e-invoice business rule code (EN 16931 BR-*, BR-CO-*, XRechnung BR-DE-*, Peppol PEPPOL-EN16931-*): official text (with an English translation for German-only rules), plain-language meaning, severity, the fields (BT/BG) involved and a link to the reference page.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_einvoice · Private data: validate_einvoice, create_einvoice · Public sink: create_einvoice · Destructive: validate_einvoice, check_leitweg_id, read_invoice_pdf.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_einvoice · Private data: validate_einvoice, create_einvoice · Public sink: create_einvoice · Destructive: validate_einvoice, check_leitweg_id, read_invoice_pdf

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
